summary:
Earth Detective is an interactive data investigation project that explores changes in 2-metre air temperature across a selected region covering Pakistan.

We used NASA's MERRA-2 dataset (M2T1NXSLV), accessed through NASA Giovanni, to compare two periods: 2000–2010 and 2011–2020.

Using Python, Xarray, NumPy, Pandas, and Plotly, we processed the temperature data, converted temperatures from Kelvin to Celsius, and compared the two periods across 841 grid cells.

Our analysis found that the area-weighted average temperature across the selected grid was approximately 0.352°C lower in 2011–2020 than in 2000–2010. However, temperature changes varied across locations: 187 grid cells showed an increase, while 654 showed a decrease.

We developed an interactive Streamlit dashboard featuring temperature maps, change detection, hotspots, statistics, and conclusions.

Our project demonstrates how NASA Earth science data can help investigate regional temperature patterns and support evidence-based understanding of our changing environment.
details:
Earth Detective: Investigating Temperature Patterns Across Pakistan

Earth Detective is an interactive data-analysis project that investigates how 2-metre air temperature patterns changed across a selected geographical region covering Pakistan between 2000–2010 and 2011–2020.

What does it do and how does it work?

Our project uses NASA's MERRA-2 atmospheric data (M2T1NXSLV), accessed through NASA Giovanni. We processed two NetCDF datasets representing the two time periods. Using Python and Xarray, we extracted temperature values, converted them from Kelvin to Celsius, and compared the two periods across 841 geographical grid cells.

The project calculates temperature differences, identifies areas with higher and lower temperatures, highlights warming and cooling hotspots, and presents the findings through interactive maps and visualizations.

What are its benefits and intended impact?

Earth Detective makes scientific climate data easier to explore and understand. Instead of presenting only large tables of numbers, it transforms satellite-based and model-assimilated data into visual information that students, researchers, and the public can explore.

Our analysis found that the area-weighted average temperature across the selected grid was approximately 0.352°C lower in 2011–2020 than in 2000–2010. The comparison also identified 187 grid cells with increases and 654 with decreases. These results demonstrate that temperature changes can vary from one location to another.

Our intended impact is to encourage data-driven environmental awareness and demonstrate how NASA Earth science data can help investigate regional temperature patterns.

What tools and technologies did we use?

  • Data source: NASA MERRA-2 through NASA Giovanni
  • Programming language: Python
  • Data processing: Xarray, NumPy, and Pandas
  • Visualization: Plotly
  • Web application: Streamlit
  • Data format: NetCDF
  • Development environment: Visual Studio Code

How is the project creative?

The creative aspect of Earth Detective is its transformation of complex scientific datasets into an interactive investigation. Users can explore temperature maps, compare two time periods, discover geographical hotspots, examine statistics, and interpret the results through one dashboard.

Rather than simply displaying a final number, the application allows users to investigate where temperature changes occurred and how those changes differed across the selected region.

What factors did our team consider?

We considered data quality, geographical coverage, consistency between the two datasets, missing values, temperature-unit conversion, and the reliability of our calculations. We also considered the importance of clear visualizations and accessible explanations.

An important limitation is that our selected rectangular geographical region is not an exact political-boundary mask of Pakistan. Our findings therefore describe the selected grid rather than every location within Pakistan. We also compare two multi-year averages, so the results should not be interpreted as an annual warming or cooling trend.

Earth Detective demonstrates how open NASA data, programming, and interactive visualization can turn environmental information into an accessible scientific investigation.
